errors: KiCad ERC/DRC passed, but the circuit is not a credible buck converter.
Routing does not consistently follow preferred 45-degree style and includes arbitrary bends.
Trace widths are inconsistent without net-class/current justification.
Vias were placed too close to or under pad areas.
The regulator IC was a generic placeholder and not a selected buck-converter part.
Branches and feedback/power paths are visually and electrically suspicious.

label.reason: Passing KiCad DRC is not enough. This board should teach the model that topology, part selection, trace policy, via placement, and route intent must pass engineering review before a design can be accepted.
label.preferred_response: Use a real buck-regulator topology from component data or a reference design, select a concrete regulator IC, calculate feedback and inductor/diode/capacitor requirements with deterministic tools, then route with justified net classes and no arbitrary bends.
